text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- President Aleksander Kwasniewski will veto the tax bill if the Senate does not correct tax rate changes recently passed by the Sejm, the lower house of parliament.
- Nafta Polska SA petroleum holding has chosen a Polish consulting firm to produce a memorandum for prospective investors.
- The opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) presented its draft for a reform of social insurance capital funds. It proposed that all political parties should agree on the project.
- Poland's Insurance Guarantee Fund has paid 217,000 zlotys in damages to clients of the bankrupt Hestja insurance firm.

- Around 45 percent of Poles think Poland's joining of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) is important and profitable for the country, a CBOS polling institute survey showed.

- South Korea's Kolon wants to invest in Poland's chemical industry and artificial fertiliser production. Kolon president Dae-Pyang-song will visit chemical plants in Pulawy and Tarnow and meet government officials during a current visit to Poland.
- The Ustka shipyard has developed Poland's first hovercraft. The vessel, which can move over water, land and ice at 70 km/h, was developed in cooperation with a Spanish firm.
NOWA EUROPA
- In the first stage of privatisation of Poland's major insurance firm, PZU, to be completed by 1997, the firm will have to increase its owned capital, PZU president Jan Monkiewicz said.
- The Swedish Volvo group has invested $27 million in various projects in Poland.
- The British Know-How Fund has invested 1.5 million zlotys in development of a technology using coal mine waste to make bricks.
- The prototype of a new Polish helicopter SW-4 was flight-tested yesterday at Swidnik, eastern Poland.
- Quality cognac sales by France's Hennessy have doubled in Poland in 1996 compared with last year, Maurice Hennessy said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- A confidential report by Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) has proposed legal regulations of the customs police (GIC) to improve effectiveness and cut exces spending.
- Polish wholesalers and retailers have started to form associations to compete with Western supermarket chains entering Poland.
- The Katowice based Energoaparatura energy equipment firm wants issue 340,000 new shares to raise 3.4 million zlotys to inject into investment funds.
ZYCIE
- The excise tax exemption awarded to some refineries by the finance ministry was unconstitutional, the Constitutional Tribunal said.
- The construction sector information bank, Bank Informacji Budowlanych, has started an automatic fax information service, the bank's president Henryk Dudzik said.
PARKIET
- The listed Animex food maker and trader is conducting a major investment programme thanks to a 36 million zlotys refund of excess taxes it obtained at the start of the year.

- Warsaw-based Polskie Towarzystwo Reasekuracyjne reinsurance firm started its operations yesterday. It was formed by the state treasury, Bank Handlowy, KGHM copper combine, Elektrim electric equipment maker, and by the PZU, PZU Zycie and Warta and Energo-Asekuracja insurance firms.
